query: Why is learning satisfaction low for certain groups, and which factors drive it?

per_column.name: subject_format_alignment
per_column.rationale: Captures whether the subject fits the online format, a genuine driver axis for satisfaction. Row readings are sound: algebra freezing = misaligned, recorded history lectures = well_aligned, discussion class = misaligned all align with text.

per_column.name: hands_on_requirement
per_column.rationale: Useful axis distinguishing subjects needing physical/lab work. But some values overreach: labeling algebra (ED-0001) and reading (ED-0003) as 'critical_for_subject' hands-on is not supported by those texts, while chemistry labs (ED-0002) as merely 'beneficial_not_critical' is arguably understated. Mixed grounding.

per_column.name: peer_interaction_impact
per_column.rationale: Peer interaction is a plausible engagement driver relevant to the query. Readings track text well: 'zero peer interaction' and silent-discussion rows flagged as critical, solo-notetaking history as not_present.

per_column.name: teacher_instructional_adaptation
per_column.rationale: Instructional adaptation is a genuine explanatory factor. Most readings reasonable (documentary clips, kitchen-chemistry as adapted). Some student-perspective rows infer teacher adaptation that the text only weakly supports, but no clear contradiction.

per_column.name: family_support_availability
per_column.rationale: Family capacity could help explain satisfaction differences and NULLs for silent rows are correct. However values are largely invented: ED-0003 parents doing worksheets after dinner implies HIGH involvement yet is labeled 'low_capacity', and satisfaction/negativity appears conflated with family capacity. Several confident assignments the text does not support.

per_column.name: student_prior_engagement
per_column.rationale: Baseline motivation is a legitimate driver. But the column appears to mirror current satisfaction rather than PRIOR engagement, and applies to teacher/parent respondents where no student baseline is stated (e.g. ED-0005 teacher row labeled 'low_baseline_engagement'). Some readings are warranted, others asserted beyond evidence.

judge.rationale: All six columns provide distinct, non-redundant driver axes directly relevant to explaining low satisfaction, so analytical usefulness is consistently high. Groundedness is uneven: format/peer/adaptation columns read the source text soundly, but hands_on_requirement, family_support_availability, and student_prior_engagement include values inferred beyond what the text supports or conflated with sentiment/satisfaction, with a clear contradiction in ED-0003's family_support label.
